Here are genuinely quick options. **Protein figures are per serving** and depend on brands and portion sizes.

- **Sesame-soy edamame — 3 minutes, 18g protein.** Microwave 1 cup frozen edamame with a tablespoon of water for 1–3 minutes; drain and toss with a little low-sodium soy sauce, sesame oil, and sesame seeds. [Recipe and nutrition](https://dieteticdirections.com/easy-edamame-snack/) citehqmU40po8lThLD_6JvpSD
- **Savory silken tofu — 5 minutes, 18g protein.** Set silken tofu on a plate and top with a quick sauce of soy sauce, sesame, scallion, garlic, and chili. **Veganize the linked recipe:** it includes honey, so swap in maple syrup or omit it. [Recipe and nutrition](https://tasty.co/recipe/5-minute-silken-tofu) citedutHSIWsRaa_BcelSHGki
- **Tofu scramble — 5 minutes, 10g protein.** Crumble firm tofu into a pan; season with nutritional yeast, turmeric, smoked paprika, pepper, and salt, then cook for about 4 minutes. [Recipe and nutrition](https://flymetotheveganbuffet.com/5-minute-simple-tofu-scramble/) citel0nVqGlh_M2RkaQq2G7QB
- **Protein-packed chickpea scramble — 5 minutes.** Mash canned chickpeas with spices and sauté into a quick scramble. The recipe describes it as five minutes and high in protein, but I couldn’t confirm a protein-per-serving figure from the source. [Recipe](https://desireerd.com/fed-in-five-the-easiest-chickpea-morning-scramble/) citecrQU_dyCAKY2kME1E8IIP

For an easy high-protein savory snack, I’d start with the edamame: it’s fast, simple, and the source gives both the timing and protein figure. **FINAL ANSWER:** Sesame-soy edamame (3 min, 18g protein/serving), savory silken tofu (5 min, 18g; replace honey to make vegan), tofu scramble (5 min, 10g), and chickpea scramble (5 min; protein amount not confirmed).
